behaviours.summary: The handler loads the entity, and when its guard method reports a change, saves it and publishes the slice's event on the EventBus in the same transaction.
When the entity's guard method reports the state was already reached, the handler neither saves nor publishes, so a repeated command changes nothing.
The handler calls a placeholder guard method on the hand-written entity; calling the one invariant method this slice's intent maps to is left to the developer.
The command, the request body and the event carry one placeholder String; the real payload fields are left to the developer.

The POST endpoint generates a fresh id and sends the command, but the handler requires an existing entity and throws for that id, so the request fails until the developer makes this a creation slice or takes the id from the path.

behaviours.summary: A GET on the view's path returns every entity row, projected onto the view interface.
A GET on the view's path with an id returns that row projected onto the view interface; an unknown id throws NoSuchElementException, which no handler maps to 404.
The queries read the entity's own table, so a committed write is visible to the next query with no projection lag.
The view interface exposes only the id; the fields this view serves are left to the developer.
Only the find-all and find-by-id queries exist; the filtering queries this view serves are left to the developer.
